experiment_1_append_cost.interpretation: Per-record fsync is materially more expensive than the old buffered append in this local environment; the absolute candidate median remains sub-millisecond for this microbenchmark.

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.name: DERIVED_DELIVERY_SELECTIVE_SYNC_SHADOW
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.hypothesis: Because replay regenerates Delivery from durable worker registration + durable delta identity, derived Delivery records might be group-committed rather than individually fsynced without losing replay equivalence, reducing coordination latency.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.strongest_counterhypothesis: A delivery receipt is itself required causal/audit evidence; weakening immediate durability can create an unobservable delivered-but-not-durable window and violate the current protocol even if later replay reconstructs routing state.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.reason: Replay equivalence alone does not prove immediate delivery-receipt durability or power-loss safety. Keep strict semantics until UnifiedDB transaction/group-commit design can preserve the receipt contract and reproduce the speedup under crash/power-loss/fault injection.

external_primary_pattern_checks.finding: Producer must keep source+id unique per distinct event; repeated delivery may reuse the same id. This supports fail-closed treatment of conflicting content under one claimed event identity as a Clay-level integrity extension rather than silently accepting conflict.
Exactly-once operator state does not mean records physically flow once and does not by itself guarantee exactly-once effects in external systems.
JetStream describes at-least-once failure modes, publication-id deduplication and acknowledgement mechanisms; any broker remains an accelerator, not Clay truth/effect authority.

architecture_delta: NO_PROMOTION. Preserve strict reference durability now; research UnifiedDB-transaction/group-commit placement for derived delivery receipts as a separate falsifiable optimization.
next_falsifiers: Run strict PR156 current head on Hostinger Ubuntu and record p50/p95/p99 plus CPU/RSS/I/O.
Compare per-record fsync vs transaction/group-commit while preserving a durable causal delivery receipt under process crash and host/power-loss surrogate fault injection.
